newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian suicide man was "fully aware" of action.
newsitem.headline: Australian suicide man was "fully aware" of action.

text.p: The dying cancer patient who became the first person to take his life under Australia's landmark voluntary euthanasia law knew exactly what he was doing, the psychiatrist who approved his death said on Thursday.
Sydney psychiatrist John Ellard, who travelled to the remote northern city of Darwin to sanction the man's death, said he had not hesitated in signing the necessary documents.
"Dr (Philip) Nitschke, the patient's general practitioner, asked me to go to Darwin to examine his patient," Ellard said in a statement released in Sydney.
"I found an intelligent and sensitive man, fully aware of all the issues concerning him and his illness.
"I had no hesitation in signing the necessary documents under the relevant act."
The man, named by Australian media as Bob Dent, died last Sunday using a computer suicide programme developed by euthanasia campaigner Nitschke to administer lethal drugs.
A previous attempt by Nitschke to help a terminally ill patient commit suicide was foiled because the man could not persuade both a medical specialist and a psychiatrist to approve his death.

Under the Northern Territory law, the psychiatrist can come from another state and Nitshcke asked Ellard, a leading psychiatrist who edits the journal Modern Medicine of Australia, to travel to Darwin to meet Dent.
